## Overview

This chapter defines the working low-dimensional representation and initial clustering structure used for downstream analysis. Starting from the QC-filtered and Harmony-integrated dataset, the goal here is to evaluate how cells organise in the integrated space, assess clustering behaviour across a range of Leiden resolutions, and select a provisional high-resolution clustering that can serve as a scaffold for downstream annotation.

Unlike the QC and integration chapter, which focuses on technical filtering and normalization, this section focuses on structure: how cells group together in the integrated embedding, how stable those groupings remain across clustering resolutions, and whether the resulting partitions capture biologically meaningful heterogeneity. Importantly, the clustering defined here is not treated as a final set of cell identities. Instead, it is used as a deliberately granular working solution that can be annotated, reviewed, and subsequently consolidated.

This chapter therefore serves as a bridge between technical preprocessing and biological interpretation. The outputs generated here—UMAP embeddings, provisional cluster assignments, and cluster-defining marker genes—provide the organisational framework for the subsequent annotation chapter, after which the clustering is further refined in the revised clustering workflow.

```{r}
#| label: load-harmony-object
#| message: false
#| warning: false

TCRseq_integrated <- readRDS("data/TCRseq_qc_harmony_integrated.rds")

dims_use <- 1:30
seed_use <- 42
```

## Condition metadata

Condition is re-derived from the sample name (`Ctrl_*` or `TNFR2a_*`) so that this chapter can be run on its own.

```{r}
#| label: add-condition-metadata
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Recreate Condition metadata to keep this chapter self-contained

TCRseq_integrated$Condition <- ifelse(
  grepl("^TNFR2a_", TCRseq_integrated$orig.ident),
  "TNFR2a",
  ifelse(grepl("^Ctrl_", TCRseq_integrated$orig.ident), "Control", NA_character_)
)

TCRseq_integrated$Condition <- factor(TCRseq_integrated$Condition, levels = c("Control", "TNFR2a"))

```

## Leiden resolution sweep

In the Leiden sweep section, the same neighbour graph/embedding is reused while the Leiden community detection is run repeatedly across a grid of resolution parameters to quantify how cluster structure changes with granularity. The clustree visualisation summarises cluster “splits” and “merges” across resolutions, providing an auditable basis for selecting a resolution that balances biological interpretability and avoidance of over-partitioning [@traag2019leiden, @zappia2018clustree].

```{r}
#| label: leiden-resolution-sweep
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Clear previous sweep columns to avoid confusion on re-runs
meta <- TCRseq_integrated@meta.data
drop_cols <- grep("^leiden_res_", colnames(meta), value = TRUE)
if (length(drop_cols) > 0) {
  TCRseq_integrated@meta.data <- meta[, setdiff(colnames(meta), drop_cols), drop = FALSE]
}

# Resolution grid
res_grid <- seq(0.1, 1.2, by = 0.1)

for (res in res_grid) {
  lab <- sprintf("leiden_res_%.1f", res)

  TCRseq_integrated <- FindClusters(
    TCRseq_integrated,
    algorithm   = 4,
    resolution  = res,
    random.seed = seed_use,
    verbose     = FALSE
  )

  TCRseq_integrated[[lab]] <- Idents(TCRseq_integrated)
}

p_ct <- clustree::clustree(TCRseq_integrated, prefix = "leiden_res_")
```

```{r}
#| label: set-primary-clustering
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Provisional working resolution for downstream review
primary_res <- 1.1
primary_col <- sprintf("leiden_res_%.1f", primary_res)

stopifnot(primary_col %in% colnames(TCRseq_integrated@meta.data))

TCRseq_integrated$cluster_primary <- as.factor(TCRseq_integrated@meta.data[[primary_col]])
Idents(TCRseq_integrated) <- "cluster_primary"
```

To guide selection of a provisional high-resolution working clustering was selected, Leiden clustering was repeated across a grid of resolution parameters and summarised using clustree. This representation shows how clusters split and persist as resolution increases, allowing identification of stable cluster structure while avoiding unnecessary over-partitioning. Resolutions were evaluated based on cluster stability, biological interpretability, and consistency with marker gene expression.

```{r}
#| label: fig-clustree-leiden
#| fig-cap: "Clustree visualisation of Leiden clustering across a resolution sweep (0.1–1.2)."
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-dpi: 300

p_ct

```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cluster-sample-composition
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tbl-cap: "Cell counts per sample for the provisional working clustering."

comp_tab <- table(
  Cluster = TCRseq_integrated$cluster_primary,
  Sample  = TCRseq_integrated$orig.ident
)

knitr::kable(as.data.frame.matrix(comp_tab))
```

Because cell recovery differed across samples and conditions in the QC-filtered dataset, cluster composition was interpreted descriptively at this stage and not as formal evidence of differential abundance.

```{r}
saveRDS(

  file = "data/TCRseq_integrated_cluster_primary_res1.1.rds"
)

```

## 3D UMAP

```{r}
#| label: umap-3d-calculation
#| message: false
#| warning: false

TCRseq_integrated <- Seurat::RunUMAP(
  TCRseq_integrated,
  reduction = "harmony",
  dims = dims_use,
  n.components = 3,
  reduction.name = "umap3d",
  reduction.key  = "UMAP3D_",
  seed.use = seed_use
)

```

```{r}
#| label: fig-umap3d-by-cluster-res1.1
#| fig-cap: "Interactive 3D UMAP coloured by Leiden clusters at resolution 1.1."
#| message: false
#| warning: false

umap_df <- as.data.frame(Seurat::Embeddings(TCRseq_integrated, reduction = "umap3d"))
colnames(umap_df)[1:3] <- c("UMAP_1","UMAP_2","UMAP_3")
umap_df$cluster <- TCRseq_integrated$cluster_primary

plotly::plot_ly(
  umap_df,
  x = ~UMAP_1, y = ~UMAP_2, z = ~UMAP_3,
  color = ~cluster,
  type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers",
  marker = list(size = 2)
)

```

## Marker gene identification for the provisional working clustering

These marker genes were used as descriptive cluster-defining features to support downstream annotation and were not interpreted as condition-level differential expression results.

```{r}
#| label: find-markers-primary
#| message: false
#| warning: false

DefaultAssay(TCRseq_integrated) <- "SCT"
Idents(TCRseq_integrated) <- "cluster_primary"

# Ensure all SCT models reference the same raw UMI assay
# (required when multiple SCT models were created across samples)

for (i in seq_along(TCRseq_integrated[["SCT"]]@SCTModel.list)) {
  slot(TCRseq_integrated[["SCT"]]@SCTModel.list[[i]], "umi.assay") <- "RNA2"
}

# Run sequentially to avoid future.globals.maxSize errors
future::plan("sequential")

# Re-correct SCT counts across models prior to DE testing
TCRseq_integrated <- PrepSCTFindMarkers(
  TCRseq_integrated,
  assay = "SCT",
  verbose = TRUE
)

# Identify cluster markers
DEGS_cluster_primary <- FindAllMarkers(
  object = TCRseq_integrated,
  assay = "SCT",
  test.use = "wilcox",
  logfc.threshold = 0.1,
  min.pct = 0.05,
  only.pos = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: save-degs-primary
#| message: false
#| warning: false

saveRDS(DEGS_cluster_primary, file = "data/DEGS_cluster_primary_res1.1.rds")
readr::write_csv(DEGS_cluster_primary, file = "data/DEGS_cluster_primary_res1.1.csv")

saveRDS(
  TCRseq_integrated,
  file = "data/TCRseq_integrated_cluster_primary.rds"
)
```

## Summary

- **Embedding.** PCA before Harmony shows some mouse-related structure. After Harmony, all eight mice occupy the same regions of the UMAP. Both treatment arms cover the same overall landscape, but the TNFR2a arm is visibly denser in the Treg and cycling regions, which is the first hint of a treatment-driven shift in composition.
- **Resolution sweep.** The Leiden sweep [@traag2019leiden] summarised with clustree [@zappia2018clustree] shows a stable coarse structure (naive, Treg, effector and cycling compartments) that splits progressively as resolution increases. Resolution 1.1 (17 clusters) was kept as a deliberately granular working partition. Over-partitioned clusters are merged in the refinement chapter.
- **Cell cycle.** Cycling cells form a distinct island. Elsewhere in the embedding, cell-cycle phase is mixed, consistent with the regression in the previous chapter.
- **Markers.** Cluster markers from `FindAllMarkers` (on SCT data, after `PrepSCTFindMarkers`) are descriptive features for annotation and are not used as evidence of treatment effects.
